results.summary_before: The Minibyte CPU is a simple 8-bit processor featuring a custom RISC instruction set, built-in design-for-test features, and an optional demo ROM for easy testing. It exposes debug output select lines, halt control, and a register enable, along with an 8-bit data bus and address/write-enable outputs. The design was created primarily as a learning and reference project to gain familiarity with Verilog. It requires some external hardware to run the demo ROM.

The input is on ua[1] and the output on ua[0], and it is tested by applying a signal with a generator and observing the polarity on an oscilloscope. It occupies a 1x2 tile area with two analog pins. The documentation is brief and gives no measured silicon results or detailed schematic.

results.summary_before: This design is a digital simplification of a leaky integrate-and-fire neuron, which accumulates input current until a threshold is reached, then emits a pulse. It requires an external ADALM2000 to provide a constant DC input voltage, and the output is observed via an LED. The design operates at a low clock frequency of 20 kHz and is a demonstration of a biological neuron model for neural networks.
